Many people ask, "Wouldn't it be great if my computer could write software for me? Humans could sit back and put their feet up?" While most people don't actually believe this could happen, they will often ask why we can't specify software exactly and use unskilled people to write it. Both proposals fundamentally misunderstand the nature of writing
software.

What do Programmers Do?

A human software programmer can write up to 1000 lines of code per day. At the beginning of a project, when the work is unconstrained, programmers write fast. Things slow down once programmers encounter the enemy: the real world. By the time the code is complete and selling in shops, the productivity of a programmer can be as low as one line
